title: A transition onto a clip with no spare frames offers to shorten the cut
goal: Add a second clip at full length and try to put a dissolve between it and the first: today every overlapping transition is greyed with only a tooltip, so the most common transition in the focus workflow cannot be had at the cut a person just made. The transition mock answers this with a one-click way to pay for it, Shorten the cut by the transition's length, and the app should offer exactly that.
notes: Mock: docs/design/mocks/pages/video-transition-wt.html step 10 (greyed overlapping tiles with the reason; Properties offers 'Or · Shorten the cut by 1.0s'). Code today: TransitionPicker.swift ~54-90 greys Dissolve, Push, Wipe, Blur with a tooltip; ClipTransitions.swift ~540-556 refuses rather than shortening; TransitionInspector.swift ~138-145 only warns; EditorState+ClipTransitions.swift ~354-362 Command T falls back to a dip. No 'shorten' code exists. Searches 'shorten the cut', 'not enough spare', 'insufficient media', 'hold the last frame': nothing open or done. This is building the user's mock, not a new unasked control, so no card. Place the row in the transition's own Properties section (the placement contract: the panel says what the picked cut is; a one-shot verb here is the mock's own).
acceptance: At Next defaults: open the sample recording, add a second clip at full length after it, click the cut between them: the picker still greys the overlapping tiles and says why, and offers Shorten the cut by the transition's length, as video-transition-wt.html step 10 draws it
Choosing it trims the frames the transition needs from the clip ends in one undo step and puts the transition on, with the timeline and the spare-frame strips agreeing to the frame
Command T at a cut with no spare keeps its dip fallback, or offers the same shortening; the audit says which and why
A walk at Next defaults covers the add-a-clip-then-dissolve path and passes twice in a row; a core test pins the shortening arithmetic
The mock's open question (hold the last frame instead) is left as it is, and noted in the audit
Audit written under queue/audits/; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not
